newsitem.title: POLAND: Parliamentarians back EU funds for Polish farms.
newsitem.headline: Parliamentarians back EU funds for Polish farms.

text.p: A committee of members of the Polish and European parliaments on Thursday recommended creation of pre-accession funds to help Poland's farms and rural areas to adjust before European Union membership.

The Joint Parliamentary Committee said in a statement that Poland and the EU should "support efforts for creating pre-accession funds aimed at restructuring and modernising Polish agriculture which may serve as well as a means of developing rural areas and fighting hidden unemployment."

The decision was one of several adopted at a three-day meeting of the committee, which has met every six months since 1993, and which this time happened shortly before the key Association Council gathers to discuss Poland's agreement with the union

Poland has two million farms, many of which are small and inefficient, and needs to consolidate its agriculture and provide other employment and infrastructure for its rural areas as part of preparations to join the union.

European parliament deputy from Austria Ursula Stenzel, joint head of the Polish-EU parliamentary commission, told a news conference that much had to change in Polish agriculture but this should not happen too fast and should be socially acceptable.

She said that in 1999 the EU would produce a new budget which would re-examine spending on regional and structural funds and agriculture and she advised Poland to make the best possible use of aid programmes before then.

Poland hopes to start accession talks with the EU early next year, six months after the union's current inter-governmental conference ends, and to enter early in the next century. Brussels officials say 2002 is the earliest realistic date.

Stenzel said the EU judged that Poland has been lagging in the laborious process of adjusting its laws to fit in with the EU and has so far changed only 15 percent, while the Poles argued they had dealt with 40 percent of the task.
She urged Poland to hasten this work, especially in areas regarding customs and the single European market.

Among its recommendations, the parliamentary committee called for an improvement in the balance of trade between Poland and the EU, now in the union's favour, and for opening the Internal Market for Polish agricultural products wherever possible.
It also called for steps to make its own views more influential and its meetings more frequent.
